B. Is this measure already running in Southwest Finland wellbeing services county (or in the Tyks university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Travel and accommodation support for patients far from the university hospital. Patients who must travel for surgery or weeks of radiotherapy get a booked patient hotel, organised transport and a named contact, so that distance is not the reason to choose a non-curative treatment.
effect_summary_en: Association studies show longer travel time or distance is linked to lower odds of lung cancer surgery (OR 0.55–0.60 in England) and higher 12-month mortality (adjusted HR 1.47 in Ostrobothnia), but no study tested whether travel and accommodation support raises curative-intent treatment by 1.0 percentage points.
supported_en: Longer travel time or distance is associated with lower odds of lung cancer surgery (OR 0.60, British Journal of Cancer 2009) and higher 12-month mortality (adjusted HR 1.47, Acta Oncologica 2024).
not_supported_en: The evidence read does not test travel and accommodation support or measure a 1.0 percentage point increase in curative-intent treatment.
in_use_summary_en: No public sign was found of a running booked patient hotel, organised transport, and named contact for far-away lung cancer patients in Southwest Finland (Varha) or Tyks, though Kela provides national travel and overnight allowance and Varha's 2025 procurement plan listed a patient hotel for market mapping.
summary_en: No public sign was found of a running booked patient hotel, organised transport, and named contact for far-away lung cancer patients in Southwest Finland (Varha) or Tyks; Kela provides national travel and overnight allowance, and Varha's 2025 procurement plan only listed a patient hotel for market mapping in Q2/2025. For the effect, registry studies from England (British Journal of Cancer, 2009) and Ostrobothnia (Acta Oncologica, 2024) show that longer travel time or distance is associated with lower odds of lung cancer surgery (OR 0.60) and higher 12-month mortality (adjusted HR 1.47), but no study tested whether travel and accommodation support raises curative-intent treatment by 1.0 percentage points.
unanswered_en: Whether Varha's Q2/2025 patient hotel market mapping has led to any new procurement or service.
